messages:
elaine_product: Quick sync — Q3 Dedicated roadmap item: we're trying to finalize launch criteria and scope for a feature set I'm calling 'adaptive isolation lanes + capacity smoothing'. Acme + FinCo pushed hard for (1) guaranteed SLA tiers, (2) burstable capacity without per-request cold starts, and (3) strong isolation. Need concrete metrics, risks, and a recommended tradeoff to present to execs by EOW.

samir_eng: TL;DR we can do this but need to choose which guarantees are soft vs hard. proposed metrics: p99 latency, p95 latency, cold-start rate, eviction_count/account, lane_isolation_failures, capacity_utilization, and cost_delta-per-token.

chen_sre: Agree on metrics. Ops concerns: KV cache leakage across lanes and noisy-neighbor amplification when we allow burst pockets. We'll need soft-eviction + backpressure. Also need an SLO for recovery time after eviction (RTO).

oliver_sales: From sales: customers want numbers they can put in contracts. Ask: what are realistic SLA targets per tier? example asks: p99 < 300ms for interactive tier, uptime 99.95, and burst availability % over baseline. Also need a clear playbook for incidents to satisfy procurement.

maria_research: Important quality note — smoothing/eviction interacts with model output quality (longer contexts + prefix caching). We should define evals: (a) regression on prompt set under forced-eviction, (b) quality vs latency trade curve, (c) canary A/B with traffic shaping. I can run (a)+(b) in ~2 weeks if given config.

samir_eng: Minimal scope proposal (MUST/SHOULD/COULD):
- MUST: per-account isolation lanes + reserved baseline capacity (reservation lanes)
- MUST: metric collection & SLA math exported to console (tokens, latency, evictions)
- SHOULD: capacity smoothing algorithm (burst reserve + adaptive soft-eviction)
- SHOULD: contract mapping (tier -> lane config)
- COULD: per-request QoS hints (x-priority) and billing amortization model

chen_sre: config sketch for smoothing (for discussion):
```
isolation:
  mode: adaptive
  soft_eviction_threshold: 0.75
  burst_reserve_fraction: 0.20
  eviction_backoff_secs: 60
```
This lets us degrade gracefully instead of hard eviction spikes.

elaine_product: Dependencies list (rough): runtime kernel + KV cache changes (4w), autoscaler heuristics & policy layer (3w), console + SLA UI + metrics plumbing (2w), billing mapping + contract templates (1w), SRE runbook & canary infra (1w). Total cross-team ~11w parallel work.

samir_eng: Risk register:
- Risk A: soft-eviction causes hidden quality regressions — mitigations: evals + canary + automatic rollback
- Risk B: burst pockets increase cost by X% when abused — mitigations: burst accounting, guardrails, per-account caps
- Risk C: customers expect 0-impact migration from current dedicated lanes — mitigations: migration playbook + opt-in windows

oliver_sales: For contracts we need 3 SLA bands and a clear failure-mode credit calc. I'll draft sample SLAs if you give me baseline numbers. Also will surface 2 pilot customers willing to run a 6-week pilot: Acme (media) and FinCo (risk analytics).

maria_research: Experiment plan (short):
1) sim forced-eviction on 10K prompts -> measure quality drop metrics (BLEU/embedding-sim).
2) run smoothing alg with burst_reserve 0.1/0.2/0.3 -> measure p99 and cost.
I need a staging cluster with realistic tokens per-second distribution.

chen_sre: Canary plan: 5% traffic on pilot cluster, health checks + quality probes, automatic rollback if lane_isolation_failures > 0.2% or p99 breach > 2x baseline.

elaine_product: OK action items / owners:
- Samir: own runtime + autoscale PRs & rough timeline (owner)
- Maria: own evals and quality gating (owner)
- Chen: own SRE runbook + canary (owner)
- Oliver: collect customer SLAs + pilot signups (owner)
Please drop comments and I'll consolidate into a short RFC by Friday.

samir_eng: i'll start an RFC draft and a short spike. assigning to myself. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Reminder — please add a brief entry to the roadmap tracker: /roadmap add "adaptive isolation lanes + capacity smoothing" ETA Q3.

elaine_product: Thanks — please add rough estimates to the RFC (weeks per dependency). We'll align with PM sync Wednesday.

chen_sre: +1 from SRE, will scope the runbook and failure conditions this week.

oliver_sales: I'll get SLA wishlists from pilots and post by Thurs.

maria_research: Starting data collection Monday, will post initial numbers mid-week.

elaine_product: Summary: compile RFC + pilot plan + canary gating + contract draft by EOW. If anyone cannot meet these, shout now.

samir_eng: no blockers from eng, starting spike.
